title: Clear Roadblocks Build Plan
eyebrow: Build plan · parent issue #569, design approved 2026-11-22

short.lead: A roadblock is any reason I give for stopping, such as a missing tool or the wrong machine. The rule that clears them is built in three steps under parent issue #569: the rule text, a reply check that blocks twice and then warns, then the tests, docs and version number.
short.hint: Tap a step to see it.
items: #570: the rule text and its detail file
Adds the section "Roadblocks are mine to clear" to the rules file and a detail file, linked from the existing "Evidence before claims" and users-hands rules.
#571: the check that blocks twice, then warns

Extends the check that runs at the end of each reply so it flags a roadblock claim made without first testing it (a probe). It blocks the reply twice, then lets it through with a warning line. A small state file holds the block count and resets when a new message from you arrives.

items.caption: Never more than two blocks per message, so a session cannot hang.

items: #572: tests, docs, version and QA page
Adds test cases to verify.py, updates the docs and changelog, raises the plugin version number, and posts a QA page for you to check the result.
Nothing from you until the QA page.

items.caption: Step 3 proves and records the change.

changes: Done when: the section and detail file exist, verify.py passes its checks for duplicated text and file size, and CLAUDE.md contains no copy of the rule text.
Step 2 adds the roadblock claim check.

Done when: a roadblock claim made without a probe is blocked twice, then lets the reply through with a warning. A reply that runs a probe first is not blocked. A state file that can't be read is reported with a plain message.
Done when: verify.py and verify_tools.py exit 0, the GitHub verify check passes, and the QA page is linked from parent issue #569.

wrapup.summary: This plan builds the roadblocks rule and its check in three steps, one issue each.
wrapup.changing: The rules file, a new detail file, the evidence check in core.py, verify.py, and the docs.
wrapup.next: After you approve, I build step 1 (#570).
